title: They Fled Ethiopia’s War. Now, Israel May Send Them Back.
gist: Theia Chatelle reports that Israel is summoning long-resident Ethiopian asylum-seekers for second interviews with a 90-95 percent reported rejection rate, as Ethiopia's Tigray war reignites and US resettlement routes close.

insights.claim: As of August, 1,334 Ethiopians had open asylum claims at Israel's Interior Ministry, and Israel has granted refugee status to less than 1 percent of applicants since taking over processing in 2009, per HIAS Israel.
insights.speaker: Theia Chatelle
insights.so_what: Quantifies how closed Israel's asylum system is.
insights.locator: Habteab now lives in Jerusalem's Old City

insights.claim: According to JACC, 90 to 95 percent of Ethiopians summoned for follow-up interviews are rejected and given three to four months to leave, while contesting costs around $4,000 per petition and $4,000 per appeal.
insights.speaker: Theia Chatelle
insights.so_what: Signals imminent returns policy toward a country in renewed conflict.

insights.claim: Israel revoked group protection for Ethiopians in January 2024 deeming Ethiopia stable, but Tigray declared the 2022 peace deal collapsed in July and rebels launched an offensive last month.
insights.speaker: Theia Chatelle
insights.so_what: The stability premise is already invalid, raising refoulement and reputational risk.

insights.claim: Israel's Population and Immigration Authority says there is no deportation policy for this group and that cases are examined individually; advocates say the interviews seek flaws in testimony.
insights.speaker: Theia Chatelle
insights.so_what: Official denial contrasts with advocates' account; watch post-election policy.

insights.claim: Trump effectively dismantled US refugee admissions in 2025 and set a 2026 cap of 7,500, allocated almost entirely to white South African Afrikaners, and ended TPS for Ethiopians in December 2025.
insights.speaker: Theia Chatelle
insights.so_what: US third-country resettlement is effectively closed, stranding refugees elsewhere.
insights.locator: When he returned to office in 2025

insights.claim: About 900 asylum-seekers in Israel were in the US resettlement pipeline in early 2025, some with departure dates, before entry was denied; the UNHCR Israel office was cut to three staff.
insights.speaker: Theia Chatelle
insights.so_what: Global retrenchment from asylum is hollowing out humanitarian capacity.

insights.claim: With Israel's elections on Oct. 27, advocates warn right-wing politicians are again casting asylum-seekers as a threat, using the legal term 'infiltrators'.
insights.speaker: Theia Chatelle
insights.so_what: Migration hardening is likely during coalition bargaining.
